correctness.rationale: For ordinary 3-cut K=Δ3(Cn^p), p≥2 n≥6p−3, the combinatorial Alexander dual L consists exactly of sets in which each vertex has at most one internal nonneighbor. Published shellability fixes the homology in degree n−4 with β=1+n(n−4p−1)/2. Equivariant Alexander duality twists H1(L) by the sign of the n-point permutation. Explicit signed reflection-orbit enumeration yields odd-n reflection value (-1)^((n+1)/2)(n−4p+1)/2 and both even-n reflection classes; averaging the known rotation characters plus these signs yields the four quotient residue classes. A separately implemented direct connected-triple dual enumeration agreed with the two reflection classes in 24 bounded cases across p=2,3 near their sharp threshold. The derivation of the locality/cancellation theorem supplies the general proof; finite enumeration is corroboration only.
residual_risks: No integral module result claimed; locality assumes n>4p and cannot be extrapolated to smaller n without new arguments.
